litigation.note: The Directors' Report states there were no significant or material orders passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting going concern or future operations EXCEPT the UVARCL matter. UV Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (UVARCL), assignee of SREI Infrastructure Finance Limited — an erstwhile lender to Electrosteel Steels Limited, now ESL Steel Limited — filed an application in 2021 before the NCLT Cuttack Bench to initiate CIRP against the Company, because the Company had mortgaged its land at Elavur as a third-party security provider for that debt; the Company states it never extended any corporate guarantee for the debt. NCLT dismissed the application on 24 June 2022 and the NCLAT upheld that on 24 January 2024; the NCLAT judgement was challenged before the Supreme Court. By its judgment dated 6 January 2026 the Supreme Court reaffirmed that the Company is not a guarantor for ESL's financial facilities, but also held that approval and/or implementation of Vedanta Limited's resolution plan does not extinguish the entire debt so as to preclude claims against the Company in its capacity as a third-party security provider. No amount is reproduced here.

risks.note: Management states the FY2025-26 operating environment was 'highly polarized': the year began with highly buoyant demand and then turned sluggish, and 'This domestic contraction was primarily driven by a temporary lull in government expenditure on water related infrastructure projects, which severely depressed volume off-take and reduced sales prices to exceptionally low levels.' Both volume AND price move with the same single driver, so the exposure is not diversified away by the customer mix — ECL sells to state PHED/water-supply departments, to turnkey contractors (L&T, Megha Engineering, NCC) working on the same public projects, and to private contractors catering to semi-government agencies. DI Pipe production fell to 5,36,336 MT from 732,004 MT and DI Fittings & Accessories to 18,090 MT from 22,568 MT.
risks.risk: Dependence on government spending on water infrastructure — demand is policy-cyclical, not contractual

risks.note: 'Exports contribute to 22% of our total turnover' and the entity serves 130 countries with 2 international plants and 29 international offices. In FY26 'international operations were impacted as geopolitical conflicts and ongoing war conditions depressed export demand, disrupted global logistics and delayed regional infrastructure projects overseas.' The overseas arm is also asset-bearing — 11 subsidiary groups spanning France, UK, Algeria, USA, Spain, Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Brazil, Singapore/Vietnam and Italy — so the risk is operational and translational, not just order-flow. (Export share and country count are back-filled from the BRSR Section A block delivered in the SIBLING profile/registry bundles.)
risks.risk: Export and geopolitical exposure — 22% of turnover across 130 countries

risks.note: UVARCL, assignee of SREI Infrastructure Finance Limited — an erstwhile lender to Electrosteel Steels Limited (now ESL Steel Limited) — sought to initiate CIRP against the Company in 2021 because the Company had mortgaged its Elavur land as third-party security; the Company never gave a corporate guarantee. NCLT Cuttack dismissed the application (24 June 2022) and the NCLAT upheld it (24 January 2024), but by judgment dated 6 January 2026 the Supreme Court, while reaffirming the Company is not a guarantor, held that approval/implementation of Vedanta Limited's resolution plan 'does not extinguish the entire debt so as to preclude claims against the Company in its capacity as a third-party security provider'. The matter is therefore live rather than closed. No amount is reproduced.
risks.risk: Contingent legal exposure as a third-party security provider for ESL's debt (Elavur land)

risks.note: CRISIL Ratings revised the outlook on the Long-Term Issuer Rating to 'CRISIL AA/Negative' from 'CRISIL AA/Stable' during the year (short-term 'CRISIL A1+' reaffirmed), while India Ratings maintained 'IND AA' / 'IND A1+' with a Stable Outlook. A divergent, negative outlook from one of two agencies is a structural watch-item for funding cost and access, and it coincides with the year's demand and pricing contraction.

'The ductile iron pipe & fittings production process involves energy-intensive processes primarily during the conversion of iron ore to iron or subsequent refining of the iron to finished ductile iron products. These operations are primarily powered by fossil fuels, leading to significant greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.' This is the only material issue the Company rates as pure Risk with a purely Negative financial implication. Mitigation is an Environment Cell operating under an ISO 14001:2018 certified EMS plus process-optimisation and cleaner-technology evaluation.
risks.risk: GHG emissions and climate change (BRSR material issue — classified 'Risk', financial implication Negative)

risks.note: Manufacturing of ductile iron and cast-iron pipes and fittings 'require energy, which is sourced from captive power plants and the grid. Optimizing energy is key to ensuring efficient production, reducing costs, and improving financial stability.' The offset is energy-efficiency investment: the Khardah and Haldia units hold ISO 50001:2018, and the Company has implemented initiatives to reduce fuel and electricity usage, harness waste gases and enhance renewable energy capability.
risks.risk: Energy cost and availability (BRSR material issue — Risk & Opportunity, Positive & Negative)

risks.note: 'The manufacturing process require water as a key input. Ineffective water management can lead to non-compliance, impacting the Company's operations and creating reputational risks as well as ecological impacts on the water level in the surrounding region.' Mitigation includes a state-of-the-art effluent treatment plant, regular effluent analysis reported to authorities, and, at one facility, collection of municipal sewage water treated through an STP and reused in production.
risks.risk: Water management and effluent compliance (BRSR material issue — Risk & Opportunity)

risks.note: 'The manufacturing process is exposed to hazards, including occupational health risks such as exposure to high temperatures and machinery accidents. Failure to address these risks can result in injuries and adversely impact the Company's reputation.' Facilities are ISO 45001:2018 certified, with health and safety assessments, mock drills, training, health check-ups, risk-based PPE and a QR-code-based reporting system for unsafe conditions, incidents and near misses. Scale context: 11,218 total workers of whom 9,792 are other-than-permanent (87%), so the exposed population is largely contract labour.
risks.risk: Occupational health & safety in a high-temperature casting environment (BRSR material issue — Risk & Opportunity)
